problem: Room-type navigation in unseen houses is hard for end-to-end RL policies and for scene-prior methods (knowledge graphs, relation graphs), which do not capture room size and shape or update beliefs about unseen regions. Metric SLAM-style maps only cover what has been observed.
motivation: Houses have architectural and stylistic regularities (e.g. the kitchen is near the dining room). A learned amodal prediction of where rooms lie beyond the field of view can guide exploration toward the target room. Framing the task as point navigation lets the agent reuse strong point-goal policies.
key_idea: Predict egocentric amodal top-down semantic room maps with an LSTM, use them to predict a target point inside the goal room, and navigate to that point with a pre-trained PointNav policy.
insight: Supervised amodal map prediction gives large gains over a vanilla RL room policy (val SPL 0.10) and over point prediction without maps (0.17, or 0.21 with fine-tuning), reaching 0.31/0.35 SPL, which shows that learned layout priors generalize to unseen houses. Decomposing into point prediction plus PointNav beats feeding maps directly to a room policy (0.16). Oracle GT maps raise SPL to 0.61/0.67, so map quality is the bottleneck. Recurrent map memory helps mapping (mIoU 41.45 for the LSTM vs 25.66 for a CNN and 32.92 for an LSTM without previous maps).
method: Map Generation: a Seq2Seq network (ResNet50 image and map encoders, action embedding, 2-layer LSTM, transpose-conv decoder) predicts a 26m x 26m egocentric 3-class map (outside house / in house / in target room) per room type, trained with cross-entropy and scheduled sampling (50% GT previous map, 50% predicted).

Point Prediction: an MLP takes the predicted maps, multiplied elementwise with the target-room one-hot embedding, plus the RGB features, and regresses a target (x,y) point in the target room with an MSE loss to the nearest GT room point; updated every 6 steps and frozen after 60 steps.
Point Navigation: a DD-PPO-style pre-trained PointNav policy (depth + ResNeXt, 2-layer LSTM) navigates to the predicted point; it is optionally fine-tuned on predicted points.

Room Navigation dataset: Habitat episodes on Matterport3D first floors, 5 room types, 2.6M train episodes in 32 houses, 200 val episodes in 4 houses, 500 test episodes in 10 houses; success requires stopping 0.2m inside the room, and RoomNav SPL is measured against the nearest room point.
Baselines/oracles: a vanilla RL room policy, maps + room policy, point prediction without maps, GT-map oracles, and a GT-point oracle.

numbers_note: Custom RoomNav task and dataset introduced by the paper; test numbers are reported only for the random, vanilla, best model and GT point oracle rows. Metrics printed as 0-1 fractions.
results: The best model reaches RoomNav SPL 0.35 / SR 0.38 on validation and 0.33 / 0.36 on test, versus 0.10 SPL for the vanilla room policy. Ablations without maps reach 0.21 SPL, and GT-point selection gives an upper bound of 0.83 val / 0.79 test SPL.
limitations: Map prediction quality is limited (mIoU 41.45), and oracle GT maps give much higher SPL (0.67 vs 0.35).
Only first floors of Matterport3D houses and 5 room types are used, in simulation only. The learned regularities may not transfer across cultures or geographies (as the authors acknowledge).
